 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Why Nick Bosa's sack-less season so far doesn't worry 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan originally appeared on NBC Sports Bay Area 
 The 49ers need defensive end Nick Bosa to get after the quarterback.
 He has played in only four of the 49ers' nine games, and he has been held without a sack.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But coach Kyle Shanahan said on Monday he is confident Bosa will pick up and once again produce Bosa-like numbers.
 "I'm not worried about Nick," Shanahan said on a conference call with Bay Area reporters. "Nick is going to get better each week, and he'll eventually get there."
 Bosa has 13 quarterback pressures in four games, including two hits on the quarterback. On Sunday, he had five pressures against Dallas quarterback Dak Prescott , as the 49ers hung on for a 46-40 victory . Bosa also jumped offside three times.
 The 49ers' pass rush against the Cowboys was not consistent, and the 49ers always look for Bosa to set the tone.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I think Nick is ready to go, and I think he's definitely affecting the quarterback and doing some good things out there," Shanahan said. "But Nick's going to get better, the more he gets back with us."
 Bosa's slow start can be easily explained. He did not participate in training camp as he experienced soreness in his knee this summer upon return from ACL surgery that cut short his 2025 NFL season after three games.
 Then, he was sidelined after the second game this season when he sustained a calf injury that forced him to miss five games.
 "I see Nick working his way back," Shanahan said. "I think that he has a number of plays that look just like Nick, and I think he has a few plays that don't."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bosa, 29, is a five-time Pro Bowl selection who was the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year in 2022. In 89 career regular-season games, Bosa has 64.5 sacks.
